clue.text: Vintner's sign on a motorway may surprise one

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
a bunch of ivy, a bush, once hung outside taverns to show wine was sold there, hence 'good wine needs no bush'

explanation.surface: A wine merchant's roadside advertisement on a motorway might startle a passing driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down-the-page sense puts the vintner's sign after A and M. The definition is phrased as a trap that may catch someone unawares.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden attack lying in wait is designed to catch its victim unawares, which is what surprising someone means.

clue.text: Exercises make CIA sober

indicators.note: make suggests the letters of the following words are made into something new

explanation.surface: Workouts would turn the spy agency into teetotallers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges CIASOBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhythmic workouts that raise the heart rate are a form of physical training.

clue.text: A Chancellor's steed crossing Salisbury Plain

definitions.text: A Chancellor's steed crossing Salisbury Plain

parts.words: A Chancellor's steed crossing Salisbury Plain
parts.note: pictures a statesman pedalling his two-wheeled mount over the open Wiltshire downland

explanation.walkthrough: Salisbury Plain is a large chalk plateau in Wiltshire; the steed is not a horse at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal-driven two-wheeler is a humble mount a politician might ride across open country.

clue.text: Fine quality port

definitions.meaning: the thinness or transparency of a fabric
a port town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent

explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the gauzy fineness of a fabric, and is also a Kent harbour town at the mouth of the Medway.

clue.text: Teatime's changed for judge

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the word before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's teatime has been moved, prompting a judge's ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the letters of TEATIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity roughly is to make a rough calculation or guess of it.

clue.text: Yates character wearing a boater? Just an old song

indicators.note: the character wears the hat, so it sits above him in a down answer

parts.note: a boater is a flat-topped straw hat
Berry, the hero of Dornford Yates's Berry and Co. stories
just means fair, even-handed

explanation.surface: A fictional gent in a summer hat is simply an old ballad.
explanation.walkthrough: Dornford Yates wrote popular interwar comic novels about Berry and his family.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional English folk song about a maiden going to market.

clue.text: Is man the maker of these? One of them

definitions.text: Is man the maker of these? One of them

parts.words: Is man the maker of these? One of them
parts.note: the question plays on Man as an island in the Irish Sea, one of a group of such places

explanation.walkthrough: 'man' looks like humanity, but it is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Small islands are the group to which the Isle of Man belongs.

clue.text: A secret's unfortunately lost point for 24, say

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters have come out wrong and must be rearranged

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A secret is regrettably out, missing its point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' says E leaves ASECRETS; 'unfortunately' rearranges the remaining letters. Dame Edith Evans was a celebrated stage player, so 24 is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Edith Evans was a celebrated female performer of stage and screen.

clue.text: "From wild Blackheath the warlike went' (Macaulay)

parts.note: a line from Macaulay's poem The Armada with one word missing, to be filled in

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a blank in the quotation; the missing word is the answer. Blackheath is an open common in south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaulay's line runs that the warlike mission went out from Blackheath; a mission is a task one is sent on.

clue.text: Characters I'd best drag from the battleground

indicators.note: characters means the letters of the following words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Letters have to be hauled out of a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of IDBESTDRAGFROM are rearranged. Stamford Bridge in Yorkshire was the site of a battle in 1066, and is also Chelsea's football ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkshire village where Harold defeated a Norse army in 1066 is a famous field of battle.

clue.text: Bronte character in Kent

definitions.meaning: Edward Fairfax, the brooding master of Thornfield in Charlotte Bronte's Jane Eyre
a cathedral city on the Medway in the English county of Kent

explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to Jane Eyre's employer and later husband and to a historic cathedral city in south-east England.

clue.text: Ex-king's after this

parts.note: late, as in 'the late president', means former
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Something comes after this deposed monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'Ex' looks like a prefix to king but supplies its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens subsequently happens after the present moment.

clue.text: Coarse material displaying the dollar sign

parts.note: buck is slang for a dollar
the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A rough fabric bears a printed $ symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dollar sign' reads as the $ symbol but splits into two pieces: the dollar and a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a stiff cloth of cotton or linen used for bookbinding and stiffening garments.

clue.text: You and I get back in the picture

parts.note: you and I together are we
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Two people return and appear in a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get back' looks like a reversal instruction, but 'get' is a link and 'back' is a noun for the rear of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy film is a kind of motion picture.

clue.text: Boasted, do we hear, of changing place?

indicators.note: the question asks whether a word spoken out loud matches another

parts.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to brag

explanation.surface: Someone bragged about their swap, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: CREWE is an English railway town famous as a junction where travellers change trains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheshire town is a great railway junction, a byword for the station where passengers switch trains.

clue.text: Gloomy like the director

definitions.meaning: dull and clouded, of the sky
a film or stage director is placed above the players, over the cast

explanation.definitionFit: A sky covered with cloud is dull, and a director stands in authority over the performers.

clue.text: Criticize record of this composer

parts.note: to carp is to find fault
to enter is to record in a ledger

explanation.surface: Someone finds fault with a recording by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like a disc but is the verb meaning to log. John Alden Carpenter was an American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Alden, the American who wrote the ballet Skyscrapers, was a composer of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Chesterton's man was, during the week

definitions.meaning: G. K. Chesterton's novel The Man Who Was ...

explanation.definitionFit: The fifth day of the week completes the title of Chesterton's novel and falls midweek.

clue.text: He's not in the club so ring round-the team's one short

definitions.text: He's not in the club so ring round-the team's one short

parts.words: He's not in the club so ring round-the team's one short
parts.note: a non-member is phoned to fill a gap when a club side is a player down

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes a club captain calling around for a stand-in from beyond the membership.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does not belong to a group or society is a non-member drafted in from beyond it.

clue.text: It's not obvious 23's beginning to change round

indicators.note: the first two letters at the start of the word swap places, turned round

parts.note: the answer to 23 across

explanation.surface: It is hard to tell when the energy source begins to shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to change round' swaps only the first two letters of 23's answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something murky or vague is not plain to see.

clue.text: Come to the corps with a companion

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone joins the regiment along with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is a Companion of Honour, an award in the British honours system.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive at a place is to get there.

clue.text: As strenuous as the RAF's bid for altitude?

definitions.text: As strenuous as the RAF's bid for altitude?

parts.words: As strenuous as the RAF's bid for altitude?
parts.note: the RAF motto Per ardua ad astra, through adversity to the stars, frames climbing as a hard struggle

explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Air Force's Latin motto means 'through struggle to the stars'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laborious and demanding takes great effort, like climbing to the stars.

clue.text: Part may be done officially, but this is not to be repeated

definitions.text: this is not to be repeated

indicators.note: part tells us the letters are found as a piece of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bit of work may be carried out formally, but it is a single event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' takes letters from 'done officially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A unique event happens just once and is never repeated.

clue.text: Maybe uncle has a right to such energy

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word next to it is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Perhaps an uncle is entitled to that kind of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges UNCLE into NUCLE, then A and R follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic power is energy released from splitting or fusing atoms.

clue.text: Dame needs transport in the Midwest

indicators.note: in puts the vehicle inside the letters from the middle of west

parts.note: the middle of the word west is E and S
a van is a vehicle for transport

explanation.surface: A grand lady needs a vehicle in the American heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midwest' reads as the US region but means the middle of 'west'. Dame Edith Evans was a great English actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Evans was a leading English actress honoured with the title of Dame.

clue.text: Slip, perhaps, in poem about tree

indicators.note: about tells us the poem's title is turned round

parts.note: If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem
the elder is a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

explanation.surface: A slip of the pen appears in a poem about a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, slip is a fielding position close behind the batsman, so a slip is one kind of fielding player.
explanation.definitionFit: Slip is a close catching position in cricket, so the player there is one of the team in the field.

clue.text: Music in the works

definitions.meaning: a sung drama with orchestral music
the Latin plural of opus, a work

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a staged musical drama, and is also the plural of opus, so works.

clue.text: Flotsam, tenor with Sir Henry?

parts.note: the tenor of a speech is its general sense or drift
Sir Henry Wood, conductor who founded the Proms

explanation.surface: Floating debris includes a tenor singer alongside a famous knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tenor' looks like a singer beside a conductor, but it means the gist of an argument. Sir Henry Wood founded the BBC Proms concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber floating on or washed up by the sea is wreckage of the kind called flotsam.

clue.text: This writer's in order

definitions.meaning: C. S., the novelist who created Horatio Hornblower
a member of the Ancient Order of ..., a friendly society

explanation.walkthrough: The Ancient Order of Foresters is a long-standing British friendly society.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is that of a Hornblower novelist, and members of a well-known friendly society order bear the same title.

clue.text: Strident club

definitions.meaning: loud and harsh, like a blaring brass band
an old golf club, the number two wood, with a brass sole plate

explanation.definitionFit: A harsh loud voice is brazen, and the old name for a golf wood with a brass base is spelt the same way.
